display.title: Episode 364: The Return of Yehudah, Chapter 9 (Adar)
display.summary_short: Why Adar means even more joy, a Shema guest, and Yehudah's years of learning with the hidden tzaddik, from his first aleph-beis to his bar mitzvah tefillin.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens in the 'jolly month of Adar': we serve Hashem with joy all year, but in Adar we add even more. The secret of real happiness is in mitzvos, as Dovid HaMelech says, 'the commandments of Hashem gladden the heart'; imagine the joy if a great king visited your home and asked you to do something for him. After a Hakochainik march with the chairs pushed aside for dancing, a seven-year-old girl leads the Shema. In the story, the old man teaches Yehudah the aleph-beis and how to daven; the poritz, knowing Peter is Jewish, does not search for him. At his bar mitzvah Yehudah receives tefillin and learns that they bind heart and mind to Hashem. For five years he travels with the hidden tzaddik, helping the poor, until at almost eighteen the old man tells him to marry and settle, and that his parents are alive with a house full of children. The mailbox features a girl's Shiviti drawing of a 'Tzivos Hashem room', followed by the Simcha Club and Shabbos times.
display.lesson: The secret of real happiness is doing Hashem's mitzvos, and in Adar we add even more joy.
